name: Corning Museum of Glass
funding: 2023: US$42.5M revenue, US$25.1M of it contributions; founder Corning Incorporated is the main funder.

name: Orange County Museum of Art
funding: Expenses $13.8M (2024). Funded by the Segerstrom real-estate family and private donors. Now UC Irvine Langson OCMA, a UC unit.

name: Dallas Contemporary
funding: Expenses $2.2M (2024); Eugene McDermott Foundation (free admission), City of Dallas, McReynolds gala, Belmond, Highland Park Village.

name: Dallas Museum of Art
funding: City of Dallas, trustees, donor circles and endowment. FY2025 corporate donors include Hunt Consolidated and Kosmos Energy. Foundations include Meadows and CM Bass. The Getty Foundation gave $100,000 to $249,999.

name: Nasher Sculpture Center
funding: No donor list is published. Its credit line names only TACA, the Texas Commission on the Arts, and unnamed members and donors. FY2025 revenue was $14.0M, nearly all contributions.

name: Clyfford Still Museum
funding: Expenses $6.9M (FY2025); city-built, Still estate collection, foundation and members.

name: Denver Art Museum
funding: Metro SCFD arts tax and the City of Denver. FY2025 gifts of $100,000+: Anschutz Foundation, Sarah Shaw Anschutz Foundation; Xcel Energy Foundation $25,000+. UMB Bank co-presented the 2026 Delight gala.

name: MCA Denver
funding: Expenses $79.7M (FY2025, incl. capital); SCFD sales tax, City of Denver, Anschutz and Hamilton gifts.

name: Des Moines Art Center
funding: It paid artist Mary Miss $900,000 to settle her 2024 lawsuit.

name: Nasher Museum of Art at Duke
funding: Part of Duke University. Founding gift from Raymond Nasher. A national Board of Advisors and a Friends Board guide fundraising. Gifts come through the Annual Fund, endowment and exhibitions.

name: Amon Carter Museum
funding: Founded by the Amon G. Carter Foundation, still a $100,000+ donor. FY2025: 1,387 donors gave $4.8M; public grants from Fort Worth, Arts Fort Worth, Texas Commission on the Arts.

name: Modern Art Museum of Fort Worth
funding: 2025-26 grants include Sid W. Richardson Foundation, Ben E. Keith Foundation, Bank of America Charitable Foundation, City of Fort Worth and Texas Commission on the Arts. Corporate: Frost, Headington Companies.
